saints.name: St. Agnes of Montepulciano
saints.title: Virgin
saints.shortBlurb: A Tuscan prioress and mystic whom St. Catherine of Siena honoured as a mother in religion…
biography: Born about 1268 near Montepulciano in Tuscany, Agnes entered a monastery at nine years old, giving herself to prayer with a fervour beyond her age. Four years later she was sent to assist in founding a new convent at Proceno, and at fifteen, by papal dispensation, she was made its prioress.

At the entreaty of her native town she returned to Montepulciano and in 1298 established there a convent of Dominican nuns, which she governed as prioress for nearly twenty years until her death, famed for prayer, severe austerity, and the miracles reported at her intercession.

She died on 20 April 1317, aged about forty-nine, and her tomb became a place of pilgrimage. Nearly two centuries later Catherine of Siena journeyed to Montepulciano to venerate her body, which remains incorrupt, reverencing her as a mother in religion. Agnes was canonized in 1726 by Pope Benedict XIII, himself a Dominican.
saints.knownFor: Her mystical life and her monastery at Montepulciano.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 20 April
